The metal plates are also called kulintang a putao (metal kulintang), and many such instruments are made only from tin cans. As ethnomusicological research deepened, the instrument drew international scholarly attention, especially in North America, and its Maranao name, sarunay, became the general term. Today it is an important representative of Filipino traditional musical culture and holds an important place in folk music performance and cultural exchange.

庫林當鐵琴是菲律賓的體鳴金屬琴，馬京達瑙語稱「有繩的庫林當」，馬拉瑙語稱 sar: The sarunay is a Filipino idiophone of metal, called in Maguindanao the kulintang with cords and in Maranao sarunay. It is built from eight tuned metal bosses strung on a wooden frame; many instruments are made from tin cans. It is played at home for amusement, and beginners also use it to practise a new piece before moving to the kulintang; in the United States masters use it for group teaching.
庫林當鐵琴起源於菲律賓棉蘭老島的馬拉瑙人和馬京達瑙人聚居區。作為一種相對較新的打: The sarunay originates in the Maranao and Maguindanao areas of Mindanao in the Philippines. As a relatively new percussion instrument it is a modern development of the traditional kulintang. The Maranao innovatively combined metal plates with the traditional design, using scrap metal such as cans to make the sounding plates, which shows the ingenuity of folk craft. The instrument consists of eight metal bosses of different pitch, strung on cords and fixed to a wooden frame, which produces its distinctive sound.
庫林當鐵琴音色清脆明亮，具有金屬特有的穿透力與共鳴感。其八塊凸頭金屬板敲擊時，發: The sarunay has a bright, clear timbre with the carrying power and resonance of metal. Its eight bosses, when struck, give clear pitches over a moderate range, enough to carry a melodic line. Because of the nature of metal the instrument resonates well, the sound rings in the space and it has a degree of sustain. The timbre has both a clear rhythmic sense and a melodious beauty, between the mildness of the xylophone and the brightness of the glockenspiel. If it is made from tin cans the timbre is a little coarser and plainer, but still keeps a metallic sheen. Its sound suits the cheerful, lively mood of folk music, and in Filipino traditional music it plays an important melodic and rhythmic role.
